## events_concert_poster

> Vertical concert / festival poster with headliner, support, date, and venue.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1088x1920`, aspect `9:16`
**Demo vars:** `templates/events/_vars_examples/events_concert_poster.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical concert poster announcing Northern Quiet live at Hall Mariner, Pier 9, with support from Pale Lantern and Mire on Sat 13 Sep 2026, 8pm. Genre energy: post-rock with brass undertones. The poster is conceived as a single composed plate — typographic identity over a graphic motif keyed to the genre, not a photographic portrait of any real performer. No identifying likeness; the artist name is rendered as type, not as a face.
[2. Action] The viewer sees the headliner name first (top hierarchy), then the support line, then the date, then the venue. The poster must work both at A2 wheatpaste size and at 4-inch Instagram crop, so the reading order has to be unambiguous at any scale.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat poster surface — no real-world placement, no pasted-up wall mockup. The design lives on a single calibrated paper field with a faint screen-print texture, ready for the printer.
[4. Composition] Vertical 9:16 plate. Top ~52% is the headliner type-block, treated as the visual hero (a custom display word-mark or drawn lettering). A graphic motif evoking post-rock with brass undertones sits behind or beside it without overwhelming the type. Middle band holds the support-act line in a smaller weight. Lower ~22% holds the date and venue stacked, with a thin rule above. 5% safe margins; 8% bleed band reserved at the top for A-size print.
[5. Style] Independent gig-poster aesthetic in the lineage of Hatch Show Print, La Boca, Aesthetic Apparatus — without copying any of them. Limited two- or three-color screen-print palette keyed to post-rock with brass undertones: deep ink-black, one saturated accent, one warm neutral. Type system: a strong display cut for the headliner, a confident sans for the metadata. Texture: subtle halftone or stipple, never glossy. Print-ready, no neon glow.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- artist_name: "Northern Quiet"
- support_line: "with Pale Lantern and Mire"
- date_str: "Sat 13 Sep 2026, 8pm"
- venue_str: "Hall Mariner, Pier 9"

NO: real-celebrity likeness, identifying portrait of a real performer, real famous band logos, real famous venue logos, copyrighted festival branding, rainbow gradients, lens flare, 3D chrome reflections, watermarks, stock-photo staging, HDR oversaturation, clip-art icons
```

## events_wedding_invite

> Wedding invitation card — formal vertical layout with names, date, venue, and RSVP.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/events/_vars_examples/events_wedding_invite.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A formal wedding invitation card for Ines Kovac and Theo Marin, set for the ceremony on Saturday, 27 June 2026, 4pm at Riverside Pavilion, Glade Park. Dress code: Garden formal, soft palette. The card is rendered as a single composed plate — no people, no photographic portrait, no real venue exterior. The composition is a typographic-and-ornament ensemble in the spirit of fine-press stationery.
[2. Action] The reader's eye lands on the couple's names first (centered, largest hierarchy), reads down through the ceremony date, the venue, and finally the RSVP line. The card must communicate formality and warmth without nostalgia kitsch.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat stationery setting. The card sits against a calm paper field with a faint warm-cream tone, calibrated for offset or letterpress printing. No flowers strewn around, no rings on velvet, no real-world props.
[4. Composition] Vertical 4:5 invitation plate. Centered axial layout. A small monogram or quiet ornament sits at the top 15%; the couple's names occupy the central 32% in a refined display setting; a thin rule separates them from a lower stanza holding the ceremony date and venue; the RSVP line sits in the bottom safe band as a smaller italic. 8% safe margins on every edge.
[5. Style] Fine-press stationery aesthetic — letterpress-feeling paper, refined transitional serif (Caslon-family or Mrs Eaves lineage) paired with a quiet small-caps sans for the metadata. Palette is soft: warm cream paper, deep ink, and a single muted accent (sage, dusty rose, or deep navy). Optional thin illustrated ornament — a sprig, a wreath corner — drawn as line art, never photographic. No glitter, no gold gradient chrome, no rainbow.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- couple_names: "Ines Kovac and Theo Marin"
- ceremony_date: "Saturday, 27 June 2026, 4pm"
- ceremony_venue: "Riverside Pavilion, Glade Park"
- rsvp_line: "Dress code: Garden formal, soft palette"

NO: real-celebrity likeness, photographic portrait of the couple, real famous venue logos, real photographic floral compositions, glitter texture, gold chrome gradient, rainbow palette, lens flare, 3D extrusion, watermarks, clip-art cherubs, cartoon mascots
```
